column2: Describe the specific knowledge, skills, or dispositions children are expected to demonstrate as a result of the learning experience. These outcomes should be observable, measurable where appropriate, and aligned with your curriculum or learning framework (e.g., EYLF, Australian Curriculum).

Explain how the lesson or activity supports learning through play. Include details about how play will be structured (e.g., free, guided, or intentional play), how it connects to learning goals, and how it encourages exploration, creativity, collaboration, or problem-solving.
column3:
To emphasize a play-based learning approach within the curriculum plan the following headings can be used:

Sensory Play (learning through senses)
Exploratory Play (learning by finding out)
Manipulative Play (learning by touch/feel/manipulating)
Dramatic Play (learning by role-taking/pretending) and
Creative Play (learning by creating)

.

column2: Identify the key areas of child development targeted in the lesson. This may include cognitive, social-emotional, physical (fine and gross motor), language, and creative development. Use this field to ensure a balanced focus across developmental domains.
column3:
Describe the skills being observed in the following developmental areas (if applicable):

Gross Motor Skills
Fine Motor Skills
Personal and Social Behaviour
Listening, Speaking and Understanding

column2: Specify the classroom or learning environment zones that will be used or targeted in the lesson (e.g., construction, dramatic play, sensory, literacy, nature, art). This helps link the activity to children’s interests and encourages engagement through meaningful contexts.
column3: List any particular areas of interest for children

column2: Describe how you will observe, document, or assess children’s engagement and learning. This could include anecdotal notes, photos, checklists, learning stories, or samples of children’s work. Use this field to plan for intentional observation and reflection.
column3:
The collection of evidence and the information gathered should come from the following sources:

  • Children’s Interests
  • Child Input / Family Input / Community Events
  • Intentional Teaching
  • Children’s Portfolios
  • Learning Stories
  • Daily Diary – Reflections Of Our Day
  • Spontaneous Experiences
  • Observations
  • Continuation Of Children’s Learning
  • Group Experiences
  • Extension Ideas
  • Supporting Skills and Development
  • Parent Input/ Suggestions

column2: Explain how the activity will be adapted to meet the diverse needs, interests, and developmental levels of individual learners. Include strategies for supporting learners who need more guidance, as well as opportunities for those ready to extend or deepen their learning.

List possible activities, experiences, or provocations that align with the learning outcomes and interests of the children. These ideas should be flexible, engaging, and open-ended where appropriate, allowing for child agency and variation based on group dynamics or emerging interests.
